cells.tense: The knowing arrives on time now, and the pen is in your hand.
cells.act: count what the ending gave you
cells.ask: Take something that finished this year — small is fine — and count what it gave you. Three things, written down. No verdict on whether the ending was fair.
cells.core:
Something is arriving and you already feel whether it's fair. The sense doesn't need a case built for it — it shows up quiet and accurate, and the same day can hold the response. Nobody has to wonder what you're keeping score about, because you aren't keeping score. You know what's owed without tallying it.

The harvest sits in your own finished thing. Take one that ended this year, small enough to hold, and count what it gave you — three things, written down. Don't rule on whether the ending was fair; that's a different question and it can wait. What the change grew is lying there uncollected. Gathering it is how the year stops being something you got through and becomes something you have.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel what's fair without building a case for it.
cells.verb: weighing what is owed against what is here
cells.place: at the threshold where what is coming in first lands

cells.tense: You are bracing for a reckoning that hasn't arrived and can't be written in yet.
cells.act: give a concrete piece of help and finish it
cells.ask: Find someone carrying more than they let on. Do one concrete thing for them this week — a ride, a meal, an hour of their work — and finish it.
cells.core:
The sense of what's fair runs fast in you, and lately it runs further out than the room does. You decide how a thing will go before it has shown up, and the deciding stands in for the moment. From outside you look like the steadiest one there. What would have been good to let land quietly gets met with a verdict instead.

There is strength in you that doesn't have to prove itself to be useful. Find someone carrying more than they let on, and do one concrete thing for them this week: a ride, a meal, an hour of their work. Finish it, then stop — not a standing arrangement, just the one completed act. Help that ends cleanly teaches your hands to let something arrive before you've weighed it, and that landing is the one you're skipping.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through.
cells.act: give directions plainly, once, and let them walk
cells.ask: When someone asks how you got through something, give the route once, plainly, and then let them take it or leave it.
cells.core:
What comes in now gets met with a held breath rather than a read. You wait to see which way a thing is going before letting yourself have a sense about it, so it lands as something that happened to you instead of something you can answer. The instinct is still in you. It just isn't being asked, and the present gets a little thinner.

What you know how to do is show someone the road. When someone asks how you got through something, give the route once, plainly — this is the turn, this is the stretch that's longer than it looks — then let them take it or leave it. Don't watch to see if they do. Saying the way out loud is how your own read of a room comes back.
cells.sheetLine: You wait for things to land instead of meeting them at the door.

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room where you are already writing.
cells.act: distinguish what is yours from what you borrowed
cells.ask: List the choices this month you've credited to somebody else. Beside each, put what you felt about it before they spoke. Keep the list.
cells.core:
You can feel whether a thing is fair, and the feeling comes whole — then it goes out under someone else's name. House rules, their mood, how it has been done here. It doesn't feel like handing something over, which is why it keeps happening; it feels like being reasonable about a situation you were part of.

Take the choices this month you've credited to somebody else — a plan, an amount, a yes you gave — and put them in a list. Beside each, write what you felt about it before they said anything. No one has to see the list and nothing on it needs acting on. Sorting what came from you out of what you picked up is how a reading of a room gets counted as yours, which it was before you filed it.

attempts.check: The draft's weakest claim is that the Too Much person is guarding against a reckoning that has not happened yet — the record supports only that the felt sense of fairness is running ahead of what is actually arriving, not that anyone is owed anything or that a loss is expected. A reader could reasonably say the weighing is just carefulness about something real and current, not bracing; the ask survives that objection because counting what an ending gave you works whether the ending is past, present, or only anticipated, and it requires no one else. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any version of 'what was spilled against what still stands' — I have kept it out of the cells entirely.
